items.name: Arya Vaidya Sala, Kottakkal
items.inpatient: Yes: five hospitals with over 400 beds in all, including a free Charitable Hospital (since 1924) and the Ayurvedic Hospital & Research Centre (since 1954)
items.outpatient: Yes, at Kottakkal and at branches across India
treatments: Classical Panchakarma with Kerala therapies (Pizhichil, Njavarakizhi, Shirodhara, Kativasti)
Free consultation and treatment for poor patients at the Charitable Hospital
Own medicines made in its factories
items.note: Founded by Vaidyaratnam P. S. Varier; run as a charitable trust since 1944. Often considered the best-known name in Kerala Ayurveda.

items.name: Government Ayurveda College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram
items.inpatient: Yes: college hospital, plus a Panchakarma hospital and a women and children's hospital
items.outpatient: Yes, with department and special clinics
treatments: General Ayurveda (Kayachikitsa), surgery (Shalya), eye and ENT (Shalakya)
items.note: Founded by the Maharaja of Travancore; one of the oldest Ayurveda colleges in India. Government rates.

items.name: Government Ayurveda Medical College & Hospital, Mysuru
items.note: One of India's oldest Ayurveda teaching institutions. Government rates.

items.name: Sitaram Ayurveda Speciality Hospital, Thrissur
items.note: Founded in 1921 under the patronage of the Maharaja of Cochin; also runs wellness retreats.

items.name: Faculty of Ayurveda, Banaras Hindu University
items.inpatient: Yes, through the university's Sir Sunderlal Hospital
treatments: Ayurveda departments within a large integrated university hospital
Panchakarma, Kayachikitsa, Shalya and other specialities
items.note: Its Ayurvedic College opened in 1927 with an integrated Ayurveda-plus-modern-medicine course; modern medicine is on the same campus.

items.name: Arya Vaidya Pharmacy (AVP) & Arya Vaidya Chikitsalayam
items.note: Founded by P. V. Rama Variar. Pioneered Ayurveda arthritis research: a WHO/ICMR rheumatoid arthritis study from 1977 and a trial with UCLA comparing Ayurveda with methotrexate.

items.name: Vaidyaratnam Nursing Home (Ashtavaidyan Thaikkattu Mooss)
items.note: Run by the Thaikkattu Mooss family, one of Kerala's eight hereditary Ashtavaidya physician families. Also has an Ayurveda museum on site.

items.name: Institute of Teaching & Research in Ayurveda (ITRA)
items.note: Grew from India's first postgraduate Ayurveda centre (1956); became the first Institute of National Importance in AYUSH in 2020.

items.name: SDM College of Ayurveda Hospital, Udupi
items.inpatient: Yes: about 430 beds including the Rathnashree Arogyadhama Panchakarma and Yoga centre (NABH-accredited)
items.note: Established in 1958; economically priced; one of Karnataka's leading Ayurveda hospitals.

items.name: National Ayurveda Research Institute for Panchakarma (CCRAS)
items.note: The government's national Panchakarma research hospital, on the Bharathapuzha river.

items.name: National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA)
treatments: Free medicines, lab tests and Panchakarma for general-ward inpatients
items.note: Roots in an Ayurveda department from 1865 and a 1946 college; very low-cost government care.

items.name: All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA)
items.place: Sarita Vihar, New Delhi (also AIIA Goa)
treatments: Kaumarabhritya (children), including autism; AIIA Goa runs the PRAYAS centre for neurodevelopmental disorders
items.note: India's apex Ayurveda hospital on the AIIMS model. Not old, but included because it leads national research and specialised clinics.

items.name: The Ayurvedic Institute (Vasant Lad)
treatments: Panchakarma programmes with an Ayurvedic consultant
items.note: One of the first Ayurveda schools in the US, founded by Dr Vasant Lad, former medical director of an Ayurveda hospital in Pune. In the US, Ayurveda is a wellness service, not licensed medical treatment.
